successCriteria.text: Initializing or tracking a folder writes its agent instructions: the six role guides under `.claude/skills/darkmechanicus-*`, and a Dark Mechanicus block in `CLAUDE.md` and in `AGENTS.md` stating the working model (the session is the orchestrator; check the role first; a subagent per ticket; keep going until the checkpoint; light tickets, slow checks in their own ticket, the full Definition of Done at the checkpoint; planner only to plan).

When the installed app ships a newer instructions version, every tracked, initialized folder is updated automatically the next time the app opens or the folder is tracked, without a button press; a folder can opt out from its folder home.

Only Dark Mechanicus-owned content changes. Text outside the block in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md is preserved byte for byte, including line endings. Files that are already current aren't rewritten. Symbolic links and paths outside the repository are refused. Nothing is committed.

Every sync is traceable: a Git-tracked file under `.darkmechanicus/` records the instructions version, the sync time and each file written with its hash, and the folder home shows the version and what the last sync changed.

A session that can't run epics says so on its first call. `get_capabilities` for a planner session reports `canRunEpics: false` with how to fix it. The folder home warns when `.mcp.json` connects Claude Code as a planner and offers a one-click switch to orchestrator.
lint, typecheck, test, deadcode and build pass at the checkpoint, and the sprint's Fireguard ticket is accepted with no F grade.

epic.title: Keep every tracked repository's agent instructions in sync with the app

bundle.rationale:
**Why one sprint.** The work is small and chained: block functions, then the sync, then the record, then the automatic runs and the capabilities hint, then the docs. The Claude Code card warning is independent and can start first, alongside the block functions.

**Order (rows):** (1) block functions, Claude Code card warning; (2) sync; (3) record; (4) automatic sync with the folder-home section, and the capabilities hint; (5) docs and this repository's own sync; then the sprint's Fireguard ticket and the acceptance ticket.

**Cadence.** Tickets run targeted checks only. Fireguard runs once, in its own ticket. The full gate runs once, in the acceptance ticket, which also squashes the sprint into one commit on `agent-instructions-sync`.

**Assumptions**
- Host files are `CLAUDE.md` (Claude Code) and `AGENTS.md` (Codex, Cursor and other hosts that read it), plus the existing `.claude/skills/darkmechanicus-*`. Other per-host files are out of scope.
- The working-model text is provider-neutral, because it goes to every host.
- The instructions share `SKILLS_VERSION`. If the Scrum cadence epic's DM-28 bumps it first, take the next minor version at implementation time.
- Automatic sync is on by default with a per-folder opt-out, because the person asked for it to happen without remembering.
- Dark Mechanicus never commits. The record under `.darkmechanicus/` makes every change reviewable in Git.
- Edits inside the managed block are replaced on sync. The block's first line says so.
- The hand-written `CLAUDE.md` of 2026-10-03 in this repository is the starting text for the working model.

exitCriteria.text: The acceptance ticket verified each item end to end in a dev build, using scratch folders outside this repository.
The full gate passed on the combined branch, and the sprint's Fireguard ticket was accepted with no F grade.
The sprint landed as one squashed commit on agent-instructions-sync.

sprints.goal: Every tracked repository gets the working model and the role guides, keeps them current automatically, and records each sync in Git. A session that can't run epics says so on its first call.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The working-model text covers each rule above and passes the vendor-word guard. A test pins its required phrases: `get_capabilities`, `--role orchestrator`, `subagent`, `never do a ticket yourself` and `checkpoint`.

`mergeInstructionsBlock` replaces an existing block, appends to a file that has none, and returns just the block for a missing file. In each case the text outside the block is byte-identical, including a CRLF file.
Merging the same version twice reports `changed: false`. Unbalanced or repeated markers fail with `invalid_input` and change nothing.
`SKILLS_VERSION` is one minor version higher. The tests were written first and failed before the change, and the touched tests and typecheck pass.

tickets.body:
Size: **small**. Effort: medium.

Add the working model as shipped text, next to the role guides, and the pure functions that put it into a host file.

- **Source:** `instructions/working-model.md`, bundled with `?raw` the way `src/mcp/skills.ts` bundles `skills/*.md`. It's provider-neutral, guarded by the same vendor-word check as `src/mcp/skills.test.ts`. Start from the hand-written `CLAUDE.md` of 2026-10-03 in this repository. It says:
  - The agent session the person works with is the Dark Mechanicus orchestrator. It plans when asked to plan, and runs epics when asked to run them, in that same session.
  - Call `get_capabilities` first. If the role can't run epics and the person asked to run one, the first reply says only that, plus the fix: restart the session with `--role orchestrator`. Don't work around it.
  - Running an epic: start the run or pick up the queued one. For each ready ticket, claim it, start a subagent as its worker, review the result, and accept or reject it. Never do a ticket yourself. Keep going without asking until the sprint checkpoint, where the person approves in the desktop app.
  - Light tickets: each ticket runs only targeted checks. A slow check gets its own ticket in each sprint. The full Definition of Done runs once, at the checkpoint.
  - Use the planner role only to plan an epic.
  - The role guides are the `darkmechanicus-*` skills.
- **Version:** the instructions share `SKILLS_VERSION` (`src/core/version.ts`). Bump it by one minor version.
- **Block**, in `src/core/instructions/` (pure functions, no I/O):
  - `renderInstructionsBlock(version, body)` returns the text between `<!-- darkmechanicus:begin v<version> -->` and `<!-- darkmechanicus:end -->`. Its first line says the block is managed by Dark Mechanicus and that edits inside it are replaced on sync.
  - `mergeInstructionsBlock(existing: string | null, block)` returns `{ text, changed, previousVersion }`. It replaces the one existing block, appends the block after a blank line when there isn't one, and returns just the block for a missing file. Every byte outside the block is kept, and the file's own line endings are used, so CRLF stays CRLF. Unbalanced or repeated markers fail with `invalid_input`.
  - `readInstructionsVersion(text)` returns the version in the begin marker, or null.

**Checks for this ticket:** the new unit tests and typecheck.

reasoning.rationale: Small pure functions, but marker parsing and byte-exact preservation, including CRLF, need careful cases.

expectedArtifacts: src/core/instructions/ (block rendering and merging, with tests)

acceptanceCriteria.text: On a repository with none of the files, the sync writes the six skills, `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`, and reports all eight as written.

With existing `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` holding their own content, only the block changes. A test compares the text outside the block byte for byte.
A symbolic link at `.claude`, at a skill folder, or at `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` is refused with `unsafe_path` before anything is written.
The tests were written first and failed before the change, and the touched tests and typecheck pass.

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**. Effort: medium.

Replace the one-shot skill installer with a sync that brings a repository's agent instructions to the app's version. Today that's `src/main/desktop/skillInstall.ts`, wired through `installSkills` in `bootstrap.ts:85` and `handlers.ts:193`.

`syncAgentInstructions(repoRoot)` in `src/main/desktop/`:
- Writes the six role guides to `.claude/skills/darkmechanicus-<name>/SKILL.md`, each ending with a `<!-- darkmechanicus v<version> -->` line.
- Merges the working-model block into `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` at the repository root with `mergeInstructionsBlock`.
- Writes a file only when its content changes. Returns `{ version, previousVersion, written, unchanged }` with forward-slash relative paths. `previousVersion` is the lowest version found in the managed files, or null.
- Keeps every safety rule of `skillInstall.ts`: fixed paths only, symbolic links and junctions refused at every level, resolved paths kept inside the repository, nothing executed, nothing committed. Reuse its `SkillFs` seam for tests.
- Deletes nothing, including skill folders a newer version no longer ships.

**Checks for this ticket:** the targeted tests for the sync and its IPC handler, plus typecheck.

reasoning.rationale: Writes files into untrusted repositories, so the path-safety rules and idempotence need careful handling.

acceptanceCriteria.text: After a sync that wrote files, the record holds the version, the sync time, and every managed file with its SHA-256, sorted by path.
A sync that wrote nothing leaves the record byte-identical.
`reconcile_repository` with the record present reports no rejection, and a missing or malformed record reads as null.
The tests were written first and failed before the change, and the touched tests and typecheck pass.

tickets.body:
Size: **small**. Effort: low.

Make every sync visible in Git history and code review.

- After a sync that wrote at least one file, write `.darkmechanicus/agent-instructions.json`: `{ format: "darkmechanicus.agent-instructions", formatVersion: 1, version, syncedAt, files: [{ path, sha256 }] }`. It lists every file the sync manages, sorted by path. A sync that wrote nothing leaves the record alone, so it changes only when the instructions did.
- Add `readAgentInstructionsRecord(repoRoot)` for the folder home and for `get_capabilities`. A missing or malformed record reads as null, never as an error.
- Reconcile and the importer must ignore the record. Add a test that `reconcile_repository` with the record present reports no rejection.
- Use the sync's safe-path rules. Write stable key order and a trailing newline, so diffs stay small.

**Checks for this ticket:** the targeted tests and typecheck.

reasoning.rationale: A small JSON record written after the sync, following existing portable-file patterns.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Initializing a folder, and tracking an initialized one, each run the sync once. A folder that isn't initialized is never synced.
At app start, only tracked, initialized, opted-in folders whose recorded version is missing or older are synced. The others aren't touched.
Turning the toggle off stops automatic syncs for that folder and survives an app restart. **Sync now** still works.
The folder home shows the repository and app versions, the last sync time and the files changed. A failed sync shows an error toast, and the other folders still sync.
The tests were written first and failed before the change, and the touched tests and typecheck pass.

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**. Effort: medium.

No button to remember.

- **When it runs:**
  - right after **Initialize**;
  - when an initialized folder is tracked;
  - at app start, for each tracked, initialized folder whose record is missing or older than the app's version.

  Folders that aren't initialized are left alone. A failed sync shows an error toast and never blocks the app or the other folders.
- **Opt out:** a per-folder setting, `syncAgentInstructions`, on by default and stored in the folder registry (`src/main/desktop/folderRegistry.ts`), with a toggle on the folder home.
- **Folder home:** replace **Install agent skills** (`SkillInstaller` in `src/renderer/src/home/McpCard.tsx`) with an **Agent instructions** section. It shows the repository's version against the app's, when the folder was last synced, the files the last sync changed, the opt-out toggle and a **Sync now** button.
- **Toast** after an automatic sync that changed files: "Updated agent instructions in <folder> to v<version> (<n> files). Commit them when you're ready."
- Keep the IPC narrow and typed: a folder path in, the sync result out.

**Checks for this ticket:** the targeted main-process, IPC and folder-home tests, plus typecheck.

reasoning.rationale: Wires the sync into initialize, track and app start, adds a persisted setting, and replaces a folder-home card.

The folder home's Claude Code card (`src/renderer/src/home/ClaudeCodeConnect.tsx`) reads the `darkmechanicus` entry in the repository's `.mcp.json` (`src/main/desktop/mcpJson.ts`). acceptanceCriteria.text: Fireguard ran on the combined sprint branch with `FIREGUARD_BASE_REF` set to the sprint's start commit, and graded every unit test added or modified in the sprint. The graded file list is in the evidence.
The final grade is not F. The letter grade and score are in the evidence.
Every test graded F was rewritten and re-graded with no production code changed. This ticket's diff touches only test files, or nothing if no test was graded F.

tickets.body:
Size: **small**. This is the sprint's only fireguard run. Fireguard is slow (100× flake isolation and mutation), so no other ticket in the sprint runs it. Workers run only their targeted tests. The sprint's acceptance ticket takes fireguard's grade from this ticket.

1. **Wait** until every other work ticket in the sprint is accepted and combined on the sprint integration branch. That branch was made from `agent-instructions-sync` at the sprint's start.
2. **Grade** with `npm run fireguard` on that branch, setting `FIREGUARD_BASE_REF` to the sprint's start commit. Fireguard grades only committed changes, so run it on the combined, committed work.
3. **Fix any F:** rewrite each test graded F and re-grade until nothing is F. Don't change production code to raise a grade. If a finding points at a real bug in production code, fail the attempt with the finding, so the orchestrator can send it back to the ticket that owns that code.
4. **Record** the letter grade, the score, the graded files and each finding in the evidence.

Out of scope: lint, typecheck, the full test suite, deadcode and build, because the acceptance ticket runs those once.

reasoning.rationale: Running fireguard is mechanical, but rewriting a test graded F takes judgement about what the test should assert.

expectedArtifacts: Fireguard report (grade, score, graded files, findings) in the attempt evidence
tickets.title: Sprint 1 fireguard: grade the sprint's new unit tests and fix any F

acceptanceCriteria.text: A new scratch folder, once initialized, gets the six skills, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and the record. A screenshot shows the folder home's Agent instructions section.
A scratch folder with its own CRLF `CLAUDE.md` and an older recorded version is updated at app start. `git diff` shows that only the block and the record changed.
With the opt-out on, a newer version leaves the folder untouched until **Sync now** is pressed. A `CLAUDE.md` that is a symbolic link is refused, and nothing is written.
A planner MCP session's `get_capabilities` shows `canRunEpics: false` with the hint. The folder home warns about a planner `.mcp.json` and switches it to orchestrator (screenshot).
This repository's `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, skills and record match a fresh sync.
The full gate passes on the combined branch: lint, typecheck, test, deadcode and build. The sprint's Fireguard ticket was accepted with no F grade.
The sprint is one squashed commit on `agent-instructions-sync` whose message lists the ticket keys, with no per-ticket merge commits.

tickets.body:
Size: **medium**. The final round, run once on the combined work. Every other ticket was reviewed only against its own criteria, using targeted checks.

1. **Combine** every accepted ticket on the sprint integration branch, made from `agent-instructions-sync` at the sprint's start.
2. **Verify each item end to end** in a dev build, using scratch folders outside this repository (criteria c1 to c6).
3. **Full gate** on the combined branch: `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run deadcode` and `npm run build`. Take fireguard's grade from the sprint's Fireguard ticket, and re-run it only if test files changed after that ticket.
4. **Squash** the sprint into one commit on `agent-instructions-sync`, with a message that lists the ticket keys.

Record each check and each criterion in the evidence, with screenshots where a criterion asks for them.

reasoning.rationale: Combines the sprint, verifies each item end to end with screenshots, runs the full gate and squashes.

expectedArtifacts: Evidence with each check, each criterion and screenshots
